newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea wants better ties with China after Deng.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea wants better ties with China after Deng.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam said on Thursday he was saddened by the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping and expressed hopes that Seoul's friendly ties with Beijing will be strengthened.
Kim sent a telegram to Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Deng's family expressing his deep condolences and hailing him as "an outstanding political leader who opened a new chapter in world history".
"We wish the Chinese government and people will overcome shocks and sadness from the loss of their great leader and continue to take the path of stability and prosperity," Kim said in a statement.
"Our government also hopes friendly ties will continue to strengthen in the future," it said.

Foreign ministry officials said Deng's death was expected to delay talks between South Korean and Chinese officials over the fate of a senior North Korean defector taking refuge in Seoul's Beijing consular office.

Hwang, ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy, arrived at the the Beijing office with an aide on February 12, forcing China to tread a line between North Korea, its traditional ally, and South Korea, a new business partner.
"We will refrain from raising Hwang's issue with Chinese officials for the time being," a Seoul foreign ministry official said.
"China and South Korea share the same Asian tradition and you just don't want to disturb mourning people," he added.
